title: String Concatenation
summary: Concatenation joins strings (and string variables) into one string using +. Only the text inside quotes is combined, so spaces must be added explicitly. Ends with a greeting challenge using two variables.

concepts.heading: Concatenation with +
points: Concatenation means joining strings end to end into a single new string. With strings, + does this rather than arithmetic.
Only the characters within the quotes are joined: "a" + " " + "b" gives "a b".
alert("hello" + "world"); shows helloworld with no gap.
Add the space either as its own string ("hello" + " " + "world") or inside one of the pieces ("hello" + " world").
Variables holding strings can be mixed with literals in the same expression, e.g. message + " " + name.

concepts.heading: Greeting challenge walkthrough
points: Create var message = "Hello"; and var name set either to a fixed name or to prompt("What is your name?").
Write one alert that concatenates message, a space string and name.
The key detail is the space between the two variables; without it the output reads HelloAngela.
(Extra) The name for the second variable can clash in browsers: name is already a property of window, which always stores strings. Using a different name such as userName avoids surprises.

code_examples.caption: Concatenation basics
code_examples.code:
alert("hello" + "world");   // helloworld
alert("hello" + " " + "world"); // hello world
alert("hello" + " world");      // hello world

task.name: Greeting with concatenation
task.starting_point: Empty snippet in DevTools Sources > Snippets.
task.goal: Show a greeting built from two variables, not a typed-out string.
steps: Declare name as your own name or the result of prompt().
Write a single alert that joins message, a space string and name with +.
task.expected_result: A pop-up reading Hello followed by the name, separated by a space.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 14 - Introduction to Javascript ES6/14.05 - String Concatenation/script.js

pitfalls: Forgetting spaces, so words run together.
Putting a variable name in quotes, which prints the name instead of the value.
(Extra) Using + with a number and a string makes a string ("7" + 1 is "71").
